review_text: the problem with moral choice systems in games is twofold: first they're usually presented as clearly signposted dialogue options in unskippable cutscenes so the choice system feels like an afterthought that other than unlocking upgrades has no real relevance to the gameplay | second there's very rarely any reason to justify a choice other than wanting the good or bad karma from it | they force you to choose early into the game if you want to play as a captain planet bad guy who kills kittens for teh lulz or as some kind of saint that makes ridiculous or strictly pacifist decisions when you the player wouldn't neccesarily make those decisions | let's be honest we don't mind slaughtering hundreds of computer generated innocents in a sandbox game if it means we get dark side points for it and the only reason we ever try to protect them is for the good karma | even the games where the system is well implemented usually when it's central to the plot such as kotor or infamous suffer from these problems to an extent | but in my opinion undertale addresses both of these issues very well | the moral choice system is incredibly central to gameplay in fact it forms the basis for the whole game and the nature of the system itself is such that you don't learn about the way it works untill near the end which makes the gameplay feel very organic | in my first playthrough if a monster me off i destroyed it but ones that were likeable i spared as much as i could | if i had a high health bar or was confident in dodging attacks i could afford to be merciful if not then it was 'kill or be killed | ' the decisions i made were because i wanted to make them and i genuinely felt the consequences of my actions as the story is amazing and the game really makes you care about it characters | i wasn't even heavily penalised for not being a remorseless killer or total pacifist player: i got a satisfying ending where everyone turned out more or less happy apart from the notable abscences which i'll admit i felt a little guilty about | my advice for this game is to not take your first playthrough too seriously and just make the decisions that seem right to you but do try to explore the game world as i rushed through which left a lot of sights unseen | don't let anyone spoil it for you or go near the undertale wiki or any youtube videos about undertale untill after you've finished it |

review_text: not sure how much other people need my review at this point but i can give it a review so | devoid of context portal is a narrative-and-exploration-driven physics puzzle game played like an fps | you shoot portals to try to find your way out of various locked rooms or death traps and as the slogan suggests encourages you to think with portals | purely as a puzzle game it's a little on the short side but it adds to this with exploration | sadly compared to the low-budget original valve got it into their heads that we really wanted something visually impressive in this game | while good for the exploration angle it also means that they spent so much time and effort on giant caverns that it takes away from the actual ability to use portals to solve puzzles | you spend about half the game walking along catwalks just trundling forward looking for the single tiny spot that might accept a portal so you can move on | they're lifeless but pretty set pieces rather than jungle gyms that encourage trials of physics puzzles and the creative application of the wonderful little tool you're here to enjoy | there's more in this game than the original but it still feels like you spend more of the time more constrained | the physics puzzles really come into their own when they give you a huge open field plenty of deadly obastacles or bottomless pits and just tell you to go for it with hundreds of wrong moves and potentially even having more than one solution than to have a hallway where there's exactly two places where portals can be placed | late in the game however there's a chance to play with a white gel that you can actually 'carry with you' from one puzzle room to the next expanding where you can portal and actually making it feel like you've broken out of those restraints | too bad it's so late in the game | co-op is also good fun if potentially a little more frustrating especially depending upon how you get along with your partner and also a bit short | with just vanilla it's possible to blow through it in just a couple hours and replaying puzzles is of dubious additional entertainment value | fortunately there's modding encouraged in this game | there might be some things you really enjoy but the typical problem of % of what's in the steam workshop being worthless tends to apply as well |

review_text: just thought i'd share an old preview of the game that i did when it was first showcased at pax | fallout: new vegas lived up to every anticipation and is truly an excellent game worthy of the series | ______________________________________________________________ i just returned from my first pax where i managed to get a good look at the upcoming fallout game: fallout new vegas | the bethesda booth had demos on the x-box only allowed you to play for a theoretically minute interval using a demo savepoint and had lines at least minutes long all of which gives you a very limited look into the game | but fortunately i discovered that the nvidia booth had a fallout demo for the pc often with no lines and a gameplay duration limited only by your conscience | as such i was able to get in several hours of play in the new game | that said i avoided most anything that would spoil the plot for me as well as avoided major areas like the strip | instead i focused on learning what i could about changes to gameplay and i'm writing to share those with you | what i've learned: if you've been looking forward to this game some of these things you will probably already know from other reviews and spoilers | fallout new vegas uses the same engine and basic gameplay as fallout but incorporates a lot of things from fallout & that fallout dispensed of and includes a lot of game tweaks previously only available in mods | visually the game is beautiful | the green haze is gone giving us a bright blue sky and a lush desert landscape which is heavy on oranges and browns | traits are back | traits are special perks available only at the beginning which either modify the game a little or which give you a benefit at the cost of a drawback | you can pick two traits for your character | one trait wild wasteland 'adds additional 'wacky' content and modifies existing content and special encounters' that makes connections to the bizarre encounters you could have in the first fallout games | skills have been mildly revamped | 'small guns' and 'big guns' are now just 'guns' | plus they have added in the 'survival' skill | more on it later | a lot of the perks from the older games are apparently back | in addition opposite-sex perks like black widow now have same-sex equivalents | food items now give you health slowly over time rather than in a single lump sum | with sufficient survival skill you can activate any campfire you find and cook food or otherwise combine foodstuffs to create superior foodstuffs | for example you can cook gecko meat to create a gecko steak which is much healthier | similar to the 'recipes' for food you have the ability to modify or break down your weapons with a sufficient level of repair skill you can even break down scrap metal into lead | you can add silencers scopes etc to certain weapons if you have the parts the repair skill and a workstation | in addition apparently you can repair items up to % regardless of the level of your repair skill higher levels just makes it easier requiring less items | and having mentioned gecko meat | yes geckos are back | in addition to a wider variety of monsters new vegas offers more variety within those monsters including smaller 'young' versions of the adult critters | as well as basic good-evil karma you also garner reputation with each settlement and group | on a similar note stealing from any group even an evil one will get you negative karma | this leads to scenarios like the one i encountered below: i sneak up on a camp of powder gangers a gang formed of escaped convicts they be evil and take them out gaining positive karma for killing the bad guys but negative reputation with the powder gangers | i loot their bodies gaining nothing | except loot of course | then i loot their campsite gaining negative karma for stealing from the powder ganger faction | as a fun addition if you are wearing the outfit of a particular faction you are disguised as a member of that faction | the initial reactions of people you run into will be based on that disguise | so as it turns out running around in powder ganger armor wasn't such a smart idea | weapons at least some of them have special critical hits | for example fighting with boxing gloves allowed me to knock an enemy critter out cold | so overall i'm even more excited for fallout: new vegas than i was before pax | it looks like this game is going to be excellent |

review_text: fallout: new vegas is a game that was very broken at launch | now that it's had a massive stack of patches it easily emerges as for me the best gamebryo game on the market | gamebyro games have a mess of issues but they scratch a certain rpg expansive world itch that nothing else really has | new vegas does an excellent job of fulfilling this with a world filled with both large areas to play in and tiny tucked away caves with a self-contained story to discover | new vegas also manages to hit the perfect protagonist for a gamebryo game; the courier is a man or woman with very little past no origin and no allegiances who wanders into three great powers vying for superiority with a personal agenda and too much power to ignore | the world doesn't need the courier it functions perfectly well on its own and doesn't feel like a shallow backdrop for hisher adventures | however it's warped by the courier simply due to what the player can do and unlike some games where people will insist you're just a foot soldier even after you personally rout an entire army new vegas recognises the courier's impact | replays are a lot more enjoyable too: unlike where the only choice was a binary 'goodevil' ending new vegas presents a lot of factions and lets you pick who you help | don't be too impressed though: as much as 'good' is a little ambiguous anyone who tells you there's no 'evil' in new vegas is a liar it's clear who the villains are even if the various nicer factions have their own issues | obsidian's writing does a lot to fix the problem fallout had of a city becoming boring as soon as you realized there was nothing in it but unlike it's hard to find central marketplaces that stock what you need and have the money to buy your loot money is spread out across a lot of places and some types of items are difficult to find easily for sale | additionally some areas can't be fast travelled to conveniently meaning returning to your home base to drop off a unique weapon can mean sitting through up to four loading screens | it's a small complaint but little irritations matter a lot when you're doing this dozens of times across the course of the game | of course new vegas still has the problems of the gamebryo engine | difficulty is often frustratingly binary: either everything falls before you like wheat to the scythe or you find yourself being killed in two hits from an enemy who withstands hundreds of rounds | stealth is entirely too dependant on stats and on top of that the stats of the enemy play too huge a role | some enemies are unable to see you in broad daylight when you're directly in front of them and others can hear you behind them when you're invisible wearing light armour in the middle of the night and not moving | blocking is still a joke and melee combat is still as bad as oblivion and skyrim with the only saving grace being that melee-on-melee combat is rare | however as much as difficulty seems based entirely on high or low numbers it never feels as bad as skyrim as new vegas is not as easy to break and the lack of healing spells means that clever hit and run tactics or traps can eventually overcome anything that has number too high to play fair against | unique weapons also make a better showing in new vegas; if a game gives you two unique swords there's very little reason to use the weaker one but when you're handed a unique sniper rifle a unique shotgun and a unique machine gun there's room for personal taste | in the end new vegas is a game with sporadic difficultly and obvious flaws but there's a lot of work that's gone into making a world that's genuinely interesting to explore and play in with a lot of cool systems and interesting quests | if you play any gamebryo game make it this one |

heard of the witcher series was probably back in when the witcher was in a top list in a video i saw on youtube | after eventually getting it and playing it i was hyped to play the third | while the witcher is a good rpg in and of itself the witcher is probably one of the best rpgs that i've played and one of the greatest games to be made | the witcher is the conclusion of geralt's story and has some things that the nd one didn't have like being able to jump sprint swim and ride a horse | the game is beautiful and also fully open world compared to automatically travelling to main area due to the story in the witcher and not being able to go back to past areas to complete older side quests | this was a great addition because i didn't feel rushed and forced to do every side quest before continuing the story | the main questline is quite long and the story is pretty well written too | the main story revolves around finding ciri who you raised and is being pursued by the wild hunt for her powers | there will be many places to go and many peoplecreatures to interact with in the story and even more that you can find on your own | there were a lot of choices to make that would affect the outcome of the game later on | the ending i got was very powerful and i had an empty feeling after knowing that i had finished the main story | a lot of side quests are actually really interesting and that kind of hit me by surprise | only a few side quests are the generic 'go get bob flowers and he will give you a rare sword' type | one even has you tracking down a serial killer | the gameplaycombat is a lot smoother and is overall better than witcher | exploration is amazing because there are no loading screens at all except for when you first load into the game or when you go to an area for a quest and a loading screen pops up to play a cutscene | potions are also made to work a lot better seeing as you don't have to meditate to drinkcraft one | the weapon and armor crafting is also quite diverse | signs have been made to work better and are also explained a lot better in this game too | in the witcher i literally disregarded signs for a long time in the game because i didn't remember what all of them did | the skill trees are bigger in this game and have more options but there are a certain amount of slots you can put skills in which means the others that aren't in was somewhat annoying because it limited my exploring until i was a high level and could kill relatively everything with no problem | tl:dr it is a good game with a long captivating story and side quests that have meaningful choices ok combat great looking graphics and better mechanics overall when compared to witcher | all in all i give this game a and would recommend this game to people who review_text: i'm going to start off by saying that i rate the witcher as one of the best games ever made and i've been playing pc games for over years so i don't make that statement lightly | i only have one gripe with the game so i'm going to get it out of the way first and that's that theres a major disparity in how useful the different skills are | as an example let's say you have a choice of three combat skills which are % fast attack damage % strong attack damage or % crossbow critical chance | the fast and strong attack options are going to be good depending on how you play and putting points into one or the other will further sculpt your style of play down that path so this feels organic and works well | however because its a core part of witcher lore that witchers fight with swords the crossbow does exactly fck all damage and is only used situationally for either bringing flying monsters back to ground or for the limited situations where you need to fight underwater | a crossbow attack takes about three times as long as a fast attack and even a critical hit only does about as much damage so it's like going 'oh dear what a tough decision i have do i want the skill that turns geralt into a foot tall demi-god who eats rocks and shts lightning bolts or the one that allows him to pss his pants in the line for the bookstore | ' right | moving on to the plethora of good things i have to say about the game; review_text: as most of us i bought mafia iii with visions of shooting gangsters in my head | while the shooting gangsters part was true there where many things left out or unpolished in the experience | let's break this down one section at a time | tl;dr at the end missions: easilly the games weakest point | now we all expect a game like this to have lots of shooting that's not the issue | the problem is after playing through one or two rackets the originality of missions is practically gone | the missions break down as follows: get information from this guy steal x kill these guys destroy x killcapture this guy | infact after playing through the entire game i can only remember one mission being somewhat different | there is a stealth option to let you mix things up more on that later | however i will say that most of the missions never feel like you are diverting from lincols goal | every missions having a place a long the way to kill sal | side missions: some of the side missions are where things get more interesting such as hunting down vito's hitlist | however these missions are just about as bland | the only saving grace being the conversations with the underbosses | these make the characters come to life more and give you a feeling of being closer to them | one of the very few occurances for the underbosses in the game | other things to do: there isn't much beyond collectables | you also can't use your money for anything but weapons supplies and upgrades | so you not only never change your cloths throughout the game but you don't do anything else | no getting yourself a new suit upgrading your car all car upgrades are passive to cars in your garage new paintjob getting a bite to eat to regen your health | infact you don't even use your money to bribe anyone | this destroys the whole mafia illusion simply changing the story to a revenge plot with the mafia bit being a side line | gameplay: one of the most satisfying things to do in mafia iii is shoot people | unlike most games they will react to bullets hitting them their bodies moving from the impact and shear pain of a bullet going through them | most enemies don't feel like bullet sponges | now onto the stealth | the game offers a stealth option | i will say that stealth can be good fun but it is still unpolished | for example if one enemy sees you there is a good chance even a bullet in what you think is in time would stop everyone from being alerted | the ai is also rather dumb with stealth | during the game one of your goals is to make enough money to afford taking out sal | however the only thing you can ever spend this money on is upgrades to lincoln gunsgun upgrades car upgrades | the enemies in the game also never get harder which makes most of the guns pointless | you could pick out the two weapons you like using the most and get through the game | i used the silenced mn and the blackburn pistol through the majority of the game with no problems | the weapon veriaty itself is also lacking | many weapons only being slightly worse then the next or whole guns being rendered pointless by them being so close there is no point | infact one of the supposed 'best' pistols the clipper | is a reward from burke | this gun is actually worse then one i can buy earlier one and for cheaper unless the clipper was given to you | shotguns are also dissapointing | enemies will get knocked back by them but not only do they fire slowly they also have a much shorter effective range then actual shotguns | unless you are up close and personal they won't help you | storycharacters: the game shines it's brightest with it's story and expertly voice acted cut scenes | through these cutscenes the characters and game come to life in a way gameplay doesn't | not just story wise but also graphically which is a bit of a shame would love to have seen the whole game look as good as the cutscenes | the way the game tells it's story through a documentary style fashion is a nice touch | the characters themselves are good except for some cliches such as clay's quest for vengance changing him into more of a two dimensional protagonist | setting: it's obvious the devs spent alot of time recreating a 's new orleans type feel | every part of the game feels authentic to the time period even down to the uncensored racial slurs | this i have to commend them for making a game with this kind of commitment in a world where people seem to always find something to complain about | glitches: in one word ragdoll | enemies will sometimes get stuck in a sitting position after death with nothing holding them up | my favorite is when i pull a freshly knifed enemy to the side to chuck him and he decided being a part of the doorwall is more his style | i will also mention there was one instance of an enemy in a car seemingly being bullet proof | turns out when an enemy leans out the window to shoot you his hit boxes stay the same as if he was sitting in the car | remember aim for his apparently | in conclusion the game had a very strong start but by the end i was left feeling unaccomplished | if i was able to return the game now i would | while i still think it's a good game it doesn't deserve dollars | maybe at most | tl;dr good solid shooting great story fantastic setting neutral graphics are a bit sub-par but still looks great about hours long | bad some unfortunate glitches bland repetative missions weapon veriaty money only spent on gunsupgrades

review_text: if you don't feel like reading this entire thing the long and short of it is that as a very steadfast mafia fan this is not only a disservice to the series but to this style of open world game | throughout most of my playtime i was planning on keeping the tagline to this review 'mafia iii isn't a bad game but | ' however after i spent more and more time with the game i can no longer say it isn't a bad game | there are many factors that play into this and it's unfortunate that they are also the factors that comprise roughly ninety percent of the game | first and foremost many of the negative reviews on here mention repetition to an extreme degree | they're correct though i wouldn't say the repetition is what kills it after all gtav is a series of missions to drive a car somewhere and shoot people as well but the fact that there's so little variation to the main gameplay loop | this consists of driving to a location of roughly a dozen enemies getting out of your car and killing them all while also doing a few tiny extra things like destruction or interrogation | this wouldn't be so bad if they were more substantial or involved but sadly they all take roughly a minute to do and then you have to drive around and do another exact copy of this same activity | it's extremely grating | beyond that there's the driving | this is hands down the absolute worst open world driving i've experienced in years | it's really two different parts that combine into a horrible whole | the first is the fact that the cars handle terribly | this is to be expected as it has been with the previous two mafia games and the cars drive like the vehicles of the period would | but they seem to be worse off and harder to control than the older and lesser vehicles from the past two games | when you add on to this the second and far more egregious problem of how the environment handles these cars the experience is incredibly unpleasant | nearly every object in the game including bushes and small objects act like solid concrete blocks that weigh more than your car | a light tap or grazing of anything will instantly stop your car dead in its tracks | several smaller objects and the railroad tracks also have the ability to send your car flying literally thirty feet in the air while flipping end over end | this truly is the worst open world driving i've experienced in many many years | another mark against the game is the ai | the previous two titles never had anything resembling good ai but somehow in this one the npcs have regressed in both combat and driving ability even further | the combat ai has a habit of either shooting from behind cover endlessly or blindly charging past your cover | this leads to frustration in that the game was designed as a cover-based shooter and you weren't meant to have bullet-sponge enemies charging past you and shooting you in the back | the traffic ai is worse than usual open world fare and the cop chases deserve special mention | the cop ai is tenacious and uses a system akin to gtaiv | you have a circle of intrigue where they will chase you and all you need to do is exit this circle to throw them off | sadly the game has a habit of spawning police cruisers directly in front of you during a chase and have them ram you | this refreshes the circle heavily damages your vehicle while bringing it to a dead stop and allows the cars you were outrunning to catch up | they also have sniper-like accuracy while firing from a moving vehicle and routinely destroy your tires which ruins the car's already poor handling | add to this the aforementioned issue with minor obstacles completely stopping your car and the chases are infinitely frustrating | beyond the design flaws are the technical ones | the game has many triggers or scripts that are easily and unintentionally broken | in the past five hours i played tonight i had a mission-centric npc that was following me get locked out of the room we were supposed to enter which broke a separate script and left him unable to open doors for me to exit i punched an npc through a cage containing our fight which left him orbiting the ring outside unable to continue the fight and had a mission-centric vehicle not register that i had gotten into it or that i blew it up in an attempt to reset it | the game will often spawn a copy of something inside of itself leading to cars suddenly and randomly exploding fifty feet into the air and a hilarious series of doppelgangers of your main cohorts in the storyline | this is in addition to the dozens of crashes i've had to endure while attempting to make progress in the game | there is some good in this game | the main story its missions and the writing dialog and voice acting are all first rate and top notch | they're a return to mafia form and these highlights almost make the game worth suffering through to get to | the visuals are fantastic and the lip syncing and facial expressions are deserving of extra praise | the gunplay feels fairly good though is still a step down from the previous two titles | it's probably the main saving grace of the game considering that the repetitive main gameplay loop relies on so much combat wherever you go | there's also a surprisingly functional stealth system included with the game as well | the main problem with mafia iii is that the vast majority of what it gives to you as its core gameplay is the exact same as the boring cleanup activities you'd do in any other open world game when you're working your way to % | instead of being fun main missions or interesting things to do you're stuck running from place to place to place quickly doing something and moving to the next one | despite having a wealth of collectibles already in the game the actual missions the game tasks you with feel like even more collecting making the overall product a horrible slog that i can't find enough redeeming qualities in to make any sort of recommendation |

review_text: mafia iii comes strong out of the gate but then slows down and turns into a marathon grind | many features that you would expect to be in the game are noticably absent some are promised in future patches and while the core gameplay of driving and shooting is satisfying how they are executed in the game is pretty lame | repetitive missions for each district require you to do the same activities before you can challenge the racket bosses which allow you to challenge the capo | the activities are: kill some people destroy some things interrogate some people or steal some things | nothing else | the game does contain some very notable bright spots | the representation of the location a new orleans-clone in louisiana is beautifully depicted and contains the institutional bigotry and racism that were a horrendous hallmark of the era | the characters can be compelling and interesting and the cutscenes are like watching a movie engrossing you in the story's progression | as stated before the shooting and driving mechanics are fun and even though it's a typical cover-based shooter it feels more satisfying as you use your pistol to snipe shot someone yards away kind of like the ai does in other games | the cars handle better than refrigerators on wheels but still lack the finesse of cars with power steering | it's that delicate balance that makes driving enjoyable | also the period soundtrack is amazing although i'm kind of disappointed that jimi hendrix's 'all along the watchtower' is only played during the opening menu | any fan of s music will appreciate the soundtrack in the game | missing features plague the game to keep it from being a truly enjoyable experience | the lack of a home base to store cars change outfits collect earn or even upgrade to spend money on kind of makes the experience pretty hollow | it feels less like you're running a criminal organization and more like you're just running around killing mostly racist people in your linear quest for revenge | k did say that they were going to patch in character customization e | g | the ability to change outfits but that should have already been included from the start | even the fps framerate needed a patch that was released a day after the game came out | why k feels the need to patch these things in at a later time is beyond me | you should not be paying $ dollars for an incomplete product | mafia iii is best enjoyed in short bursts grinding out a racket or two in between other games | i hoped that k wouldn't be patching in features at a later date but it seems like that's what you're going to have to wait for | don't buy it in its current state for full price | wait for the new features to be patched in and then buy it | it can be an enjoyable experience and out good voice acting great soundtrack cons: incredibly stupid driverpedestrian ai enemy ai is pretty shaky repetitive grinding for racketsbossescapos no character customization promised in later review_text: i try to be an optimist in my life as much as possible | i dont find it enjoyable to be a pessimist and be cynical about everything | thats why im going to try and look at mafia iii as a glass-half-full kind of game | the good parts of mafia are really tremendous but the bad parts are equally as frustrating | mafia iii follows the dare i say it underrated mafia ii released in | mafia ii followed the story of vito scaletta as he rose through the ranks of the mob and told a really compelling and gripping story | the narrative was tight with great characters but had one nearly universal criticism; the gameplay | mafia ii was an open world game that didnt need to be open world | there were prolonged amounts of having to drive from point a to b with no real reason to do so | you couldnt interact with the rest of the world and there was nothing else to see so it was literally just a waste of time | unfortunately mafia iii follows this same path | mafia iii takes place in fictional louisiana in with the biracial vietnam vet lincoln clay in the lead role | thats a lot to digest right there; late s racism the vietnam war | mafia iii puts a whole heck of a lot on its plate and attempts to finish it all | i would say that the devs at hangar do quite a deft job of navigating the themes and issues of the time while taking them head on without beating you over the head with it or coming off as offensive | their depiction of racism during this time is done in a believable way | yes there is a gratuitous amount of racial slurs thrown around but as the disclaimer at the beginning of the game says its done to be accurate to the times and not to diminish or shy away from what people went through | the characterization in mafia iii is really great giving you characters you can empathize with as well as ones that you loathe | they give lincoln clay an interesting backstory and mostly make great use of it in a revenge story that doesnt feel clich | mafia iiis story provides a great foundation yet its the games design that really shows its cracks | now i know that game design is a tough job and i dont want to come across like an armchair quarterback but the mission designer really dropped the ball here | with the exception of a handful the majority of the mission structures in mafia are exactly the same | you need to weaken a racket so you go to [insert building here] and either kill or interrogate the boss at that site as well as destroy any contraband and take any money thats there | while there are permutations and different settings thats effectively what the game is | i think it goes without saying that it can get a tad bit monotonous | thankfully the gunplay and the stealth are good enough that you can mix up and vary your play style to keep things from getting stale | i was specifically impressed by how viable of an option the stealth was which is almost unheard of in a gta-style open world game | there were numerous missions where i ghosted the whole place and didnt fire a single shot | the other design choice that left me scratching my head was no fast travel | its what the hell | now im not necessarily for games being easier i know some people appreciate hard games but what i have little to no tolerance for is a game that wastes my time | the developers here seemingly left out fast travel for no other reason than to pad the games length | much like mafia ii theres no reason for me to stop anywhere while im driving to a destination | my eyes nearly got stuck the amount of times i rolled them back as the game wanted me to go from one side of the map to the other | thats simply insulting to me as a consumer | i will say though that the driving is damn fun | perhaps the best open world driving ive experienced | so while i may have complaints with the lack of fast travel having to drive everywhere didnt really wear on me until the very end because the car handling was so sublime | mafia iii was a game that i was hoping would be in my goty discussion | sadly its not there and its not even particularly close | but that does not mean that its a bad game | the narrative and the characters that are presented are top notch and are what kept me coming back and driving literally through the so-so gameplay to reach its finale | i recommend people play mafia iii because without sounding trite its a bold and brave move for a aaa game to have a black protagonist and deal with the themes and issues that it does | but with that recommendation comes a caveat; know what youre getting into | if you think that the nature of the mission structure will not bother you then there is a ton of fun to be had here | is it worth $ | absolutely not but if you can get it around $ then i think theres enough there to satisfy | i wouldnt have played it for hours had i not enjoyed it |

review_text: as the old proverb goes revenge is a dish best served cold | but for mafia 's lincoln clay revenge is a dish best served with buckets of blood preferably prepared using a razor sharp combat knife | betrayed and left for dead by the italian mob lincoln subsequently sets out on the warpath hellbent on exacting vengeance upon those who wronged him and destroyed his family | that means dismantling mafia don sal marcano's sprawling criminal empire across the city of new bordeaux one piece at a time | wiping out marcano's criminal rackets is at the heart of mafia 's story as lincoln and his chain-smoking cia insider john donavan set about bringing down enforcers lieutenants and capos before going after the big man himself | however there's more to do beyond simply getting to marcano meaning lincoln requires the help of underbosses cassandra vito scaletta and thomas burke | as you recruit each of these lieutenants you'll gain a variety of perks like an arms dealer a consigliere to collect your cash a hit squad to help out in a fight or vehicle delivery but retaining these means keeping your underbosses happy | as you gain control of each of new bordeaux's rackets you'll assign them to whichever underboss you like before calling a sit down to decide who inherits the entire district | it's up to you whether you favour one or two of your underbosses or take a more diplomatic approach divvying turf up equally between all three | failing to keep an underboss happy however will push them out turning them into an enemy that lincoln will have to deal with | it means the decisions you make during sit downs can have real consequences so you'll need to choose wisely | there are some facets of mafia that you'll need to think about then although for the most part the game's missions are largely variations on the same objective sending you into hostile territory to clear out criminal scumbags | little things like wiretapping junction boxes using fuses also reveals enemy positions other racket locations and collectibles in the region on the mini map making life easier for yourself | an accomplished cover shooter at its core practically every one of the rackets you seize comes from clearing out heavily armed goons whether via stealthy means or through a more gung-ho approach | as such you can expect to be stacking up the bodies murdering enforcers interrogating informants who can be recruited if you'd rather not kill them and inflicting damage to the racket by destroying stashes of drugs chemicals or whatever | it can actually get rather repetitive | thankfully mafia 's shooter mechanics are fantastic as are the rest of the game's open-world systems like the fun driving model that includes a more realistic 'simulation' option that can be toggled on or off or the brutal and gratifying melee combat | by the time you reach the latter stages of mafia you'll be a well-oiled killing machine able to pull off brutal kills and headshots with aplomb | unfortunately mafia is hampered by a whole litany of bugs and other issues most of which are odd visual quirks including some lighting weirdness numerous instances of pop-in nutty physics that send cars flying through the air off the slightest bump character model glitches and regular occurrences where the ai behaves in laughably strange ways | in fact the ai in general can be rather shoddy either seeing you through walls or passing you by completely without noticing you're there | it's a shame because mafia is genuinely enjoyable despite its range of problems | the soundtrack too is utterly stellar stuff delivering the best of s music and bringing its version of a tumultuous new orleans to startling life | the tunes blaring out of the radio from the likes of the rolling stones the beach boys creedence clearwater revival jimi hendrix and others are one of the best bits of mafia | the game's excellent storyline also keeps things ticking along nicely intercut with present day documentary-style sequences and donovan's testimony telling the tale of lincoln clay's vengeful mission from the perspective of the people who were there at the time | it's a great narrative device although there are certain scenes that recount what happened before you've actually had the chance to play out the ensuing scenario | nonetheless mafia 's story is fantastic unflinchingly violent and authentic in its rendition of a turbulent time and place | definitely not for the faint-hearted hangar 's open-world is one that's riddled with rampant racism sex drugs and other criminal activities covered in gritty detail that doesn't pull any punches | where gta revels in sharp satire and humour mafia is a more serious beast not shying away from any of the issues that ran through american culture at the time | from the moment you start the game up there's a statement from hangar saying as much warning that the offensive language and period is shown as it was warts and all | as for the achievements there's a really good spread across all of mafia 's various aspects but there are a couple thrown in there that require a second playthrough | for such an enormous review_text: war never changes runs the tagline for fallout and though that's a dour descriptor for this sometimes bleakly hilarious game it's also sort of true that the fallout series hasn't really changed | however that's because of another important saying: if it ain't broke don't fix it | short of changing the setting to the boston area circa bethesda game studios simply hasn't had to tinker with much since 's near-perfect fallout: new vegas | the big new questionable improvement is basically the inclusion of a built-in mod kit which allows players to fix up their liberated settlements | as it turns out it's a bit more onerous to construct things on a d plane as opposed to the d plane of the game's mobile prequel fallout shelter | it's also largely unnecessary to waste skill points on perks like gun nut that allow for deeper customization on one's arsenal given that every slain foe drops everything they're wearing | then again this only enhances the realism of the game both in terms of the cobbled-together post-apocalyptic aesthetic and in the freedom given to those who want to play through on their own terms | but fallout is far more than an expansion | without spoiling too much the plot introduces a new creature beyond the standard irradiated monsters like the bearish yao guai and self-descriptive bloatflies and feral ghouls | these new foes or potentially friends are synths robots that are all but indistinguishable from humans | it's blade runner in all the right ways and most of the moral story-altering dilemmas presented this go-around revolve around which of the various factions players choose to support from those in the railroad who want to set the enslaved synths free to the familiar faces of the brotherhood of steel who want to destroy that dangerous technology | the core of fallout 's journey centers on your character and his or her quest to find the truth about what happened in vault | though the last two fallout games put you smack in the center of an involved narrative it never felt as personal or invested as fallout 's story | that's largely due to fallout 's committal to giving the player character voiced dialogue | the typical silent protagonist is gone and bethesda's taken a bit of a bioware approach to giving the player a meaningful connection to the in-game avatar | your story will play out with dialogue choices you selected and just by having an actor there to give some inflection to the words bethesda is able to make you more connected to this persona than ever before | while conversational choice has been a part of the fallout series talking it out with computer characters face-to-face was always a bit disjointed | it never felt natural | with fallout there's a more cinematic approach to conversations | the camera always pulls out to find a more appealing angle to show the different sides of a conversation | there's a large emphasis on making your character more a part of this world by showing him or her from outside the default first-person perspective and it makes a great deal of difference in connecting you to this person this world and the conversations you'll have | conversations are equally as important to fleshing out your relationship with the numerous companions you'll meet on your adventure | unlike previous entries in the series these characters actually feel like companions | whether it's dogmeat piper codsworth or any of the others you'll encounter and befriend there's more to having these people around than just serving as another gun in battle or a walking storage unit | the longer you hang out with a single companion the more your relationship with that person will grow | characters will talk with you while on quests and your decisions no matter how minor will impact how they perceive you | complements to the so-called main campaign aside the majority of a player's time in fallout is spent wandering around the commonwealth especially now that bethesda has removed the level cap and it's the setting that ultimately needs to hold up as a central character | those who were skeptical that bostona less immediately familiar setting than washington d | c | or las vegascan rest easy that the commonwealth is well represented | fenway park has been repurposed and turned into diamond city walking the historic freedom trail plays a pivotal role the salem museum of witchcraft is open for business and there's a new batch of minutemen out to beat the drums of revolution or at least protect citizens from the raiders and super mutants attempting to divvy up landmarks like faneuil hall bunker hill and walden's pond | and while it's nice to have coastal options available for exploration like the floating anarchic raft city of libertalia fallout is filled with other unique environments such as the glowing wastes and the airship prydwen | admittedly while the various vaults hospitals military bases and libraries all start to bleed together given enough time the sideplots that send you there are filled with more than enough variety to pick up the slack whether that means facing off against a serial killer who's festooned an art gallery with his bloody paintings and skeletal sculptures or exposing vault-tec's nefarious experimentation by finding sub-vaults hidden within the main ones | the first-person shooting also grows stale after several dozen hours but as with borderlands and destiny the constant acquisition of new weapons and perks at least provides a sense of achievement for all that marksmanship | there are multiple suits you can find scattered throughout the boston area all in various states of disrepair | scavenging parts from these or those you find on raiders encountered in the wild to craft a single solid suit of armor is a key component of becoming a force to be reckoned with in the wastes | you can even customize the armor a bit adding extra reinforcement to ensure you've got the most protection you can get | the vats mechanic returns but only slows down time instead of pausing it | i found this change heightened the risk of any encounter and made vats much more of a last resort instead of a go to for critical hits solution it had been in previous games | it also made me use it less as a result but thankfully the first person mechanics are probably the best bethesda has produced in its rpgs | visually fallout is a rather impressive game and has some insane attention to detail | from the very first time you set foot into the world of this post apocalyptic game you feel like youre on another world and whether thats the s inspired post-game introduction or walking out of the bunker for the first time bgs have really hit the mark when it comes to the atmosphere | so no matter where you look like the ground the sky or as you enter a plethora of different buildings its definitely a labour of love and really immerses you into not just the character but the world itself | the game's music is perfectly set for the different situations you find yourself in | it's suitably dramatic in the big fight scenes and similarly soft when you get to a more emotional part | whilst not at the forefront of your attention the music is always there and sometimes you won't even notice it until it goes silent | your heart might be in your mouth as you hack a computer or lockpick a door with enemies nearby and the music will do a great job to reflect exactly how you are feeling | the best thing about fallout is the freedom that it gives you not only with what to do and where to go but also how quests will turn out | will you talk your way out of a certain quest or run in all guns blazing | the choice is yours | overall the game is pretty close to perfect and if you decide to pass on exploring the vast wasteland then you only have yourself to blame | the hype is real and you won't be disappointed |

review_text: considering the last game released in the series here is what you can expect from fallout : pros: much better gunplay | much better animations in some regards specifically regarding that of player movement in power armor better visually enviroments are far more vivid better facial animation gun customization is very in-depth and makes sense for the most part | companions are for the most part pretty interesting | some of what they do is a logical extension of the mechanics presented in fallout: new vegas | what remained about the same: = sound design is for better or worse about the same | gunshots are gunshots and the voice acting ranges from superb to mediocre | =vats | the slowing time as opposed to stopping time is functionally little different except in a few scenarios | what is worse: the dialogue system is a distinct downgrade from every other fallout | voiced protagonist adds litte if anything | most responses in the dialogue system are varying flavors of essentially the same response | no 'idiot' dialogue for low int characters | no 'skill' dialogue i | e | all conversation is only affected by your flat cha score and a select few 'speech' perks | special system has been severely dumbed down in previous fallouts was considered an average score in this game f considers an average score to be | there are no more skill points or skills for that matter points leveling up are either fed back into base special scores or put into perks most of which are ranked | a lot of confusing retcons that are unclear if intentional on bethesda's part i | e | the general availability of vertibirds fusion core lifespans admittedly this was a gameplay decision jet being a pre-war drug etc | if you are familiar with fallout lore this game will not please you with its setting mastery | crafting doesn't change as much as you think | you still carry around a lot of copies of weapons but mostly to strip mods off of them or to turn into scrap | reloading ammunition is absent from nv which is a somewhat glaring ommission considering the sheer breadth of modification available to the player | settlements feel tacked on and lacking depth | the system is there but the game never really requires that you do very much with it outside of a few quests | the game can be comfortably played with one 'home' settlement that is very well developed with the rest of the wasteland living in squalor | any time investment you make into this system will be at your discretion | now on to some more subjective points | these are purely my opinions and can be taken with as much salt as you like | for reference i have played all previous fallouts only have game time recorded on f and f:nv on my steam account so you'll have to take my word for it and are very familiar with the setting and games | that being said here are some points that i personally as a fallout fan did not like: factions are largely a mess | the institute's methodology is unclear and questionable | the brotherhood of steel although technically correct in their methods and goals feel poorly executed and tacked on | the minutemen are inconsequential and the railroad does not have the size or influence to be a power player on the scale of the other factions | in short i find that none of the factions are developed enough or well thought out enough to make it worth the player's time to side with any of them and the game does not make an effort to 'lock you out' of other faction's quests barring anything but outright violence | if you liked the writing and nuance of fallout: new vegas f or f as i did then this game will probably disappoint you | i could only find the game bearable when i was exploring without any provocation from anyone to do so | the voiced dialogue and brainless dialogue system only exists as a vehicle to deliver to quests to you or with which to barter there is no opportunity to 'roleplay' your character | of all the protagonists of fallout games this one is the only one that was not a blank slate for the player to imprint upon the main character either the wife or husband already comes fairly established their backstory as far as the player is concerned for instance is revealed in the opening of the game | this was something that fallout also suffered from i | e | there was no room to play an old character because the game infers you were exiled fairly early in your adulthood among other things leaving you no room whatsoever in the game's eyes to 'create' your character outside of purely cosmetic elements | it is always possible to ignore such things as the player but to the game it makes no difference you are always the same character | to summarize fallout is a game that manages to only really be a sidegrade from fallout another deeply flawed title when looked at through the lense of a fallout game | this game is an excuse to loot and shoot in a post-apocalyptic theme park and nothing more than that | if that's what you desire then that is what you will most certainly get | however if you wanted a fallout title that feels like the original games or even new vegas then your money might be better spent elsewhere | i cannot personally reccommend this game to other people |

with a more traditional shooter gameplay it gets compared to destiny alot and a minecraftsurvivalist crafting system | everything else you'd expect from a fallout game is there still just somewhat watered down | in a sense it's nice because the whole game feels alot more approachable for new players and is simpler to get used to but i would fault it because it doesn't do any of its features especially well just good enough | combat is difficult in this game since the fluid pacing you would expect from a shooter gets interrupted with items that are too small to notice buggy ai and animations with extra frames making it difficult to time your sprint command input right after you reload ie if one animation hasn't fully ended it seems the game will not allow you to perform certain slight understatement | i first played the original fallout way back when on my parent's first computer and i still look back fondly on the many hours i spent playing it | occasionally i still load up my gog | com copy of the and revisit the game | i had similar experiences with the following installments of fallout and fallout tactics | it was during my freshman year of highschool that fallout made its leap to console with the release of fallout from the developers at bethesda | it was all my friends and i could talk about until the release of skyrim but it succeeded in introducing a new generation to the franchise | fallout three expanded greatly on how we viewed the fallout universe while retaining the wit and character from the earlier games | while it's disappointing that we will never see the realization of van buren i still feel strongly the fallout is a worthy successor to the original entries | fallout: new vegas to put it plainly i enjoyed new vegas | i've heard many opinions on what is 'wrong' with the game and i can't bring myself to dislike it | it shared many of the qualities of three with improvements to the systems and features not present in the series prior | among its most notable qualities is the use of a faction relations system iron sights and of course the iconic survival mode | i'd happily spend the remainder of my time discussing new vegas but your aren't here for that fallout to understand why i reviewed this game the way i have it's worth noting a two quick things: | i'm a longtime fan of the series as you can no doubt tell by the wall of text above it | | i have a personal idea of what defines fallout as a series and i encourage you to hear me out on some of these reason for disliking the game | obviously these are my own gripes and if you feel strongly for or against feel free to post your own review of the game | fallout possesses all the qualities and looks of a console made fallout game | we have elements of three with the improved concepts of new vegas all packaged nicely onto an engine that allows the fine folks at bethesda to really let down there hair and dig deep | from the first few minute of the game we realize very quickly this game is different | visually the game is very stunning and at higher settings on a mid to high end pc we can see very quickly how much effort was put into the visual appeal of characters their environment and how we as players interact with it | from a lore standpoint this provides a real on the nose experience of pre war life from the comforts of the starting location in sanctuary | i was disappointed when i first heard they intended to use voice acting for the player character but still i tried to keep an open mind going into it | but when it came to interacting with our friendly vault-tec rep i quickly realized why exactly i was disappointed | the characters voice which mind you was absent from every game prior | took me out of the roleplay experience and put me in the shoes of john and jane doe | from a character perspective i wasn't so much playing my own character instead i was forced into the position of a loving father and husband with his own pre established backstory | to further add to the immersion breaking experience fallout is plagued with a mass effect styled chat wheel that is in the eyes of some fans and insulting stupefication of to be a raider and some up | but with fallout i can at most be a ticked off widower with a chip on my shoulder | the combat is similar in many regards to prior entries | vats remains intact albeit and yes this is positive with more functionality | we retain the option of rd or st person shooting perspectives which is nice but if you're like me you will most likely be locked in first person for most of your fire fights | the early game benefits greatly from the improved action oriented pacing and i found myself quickly falling head over heels for both the laser musket and the sawn off shotgun | with maxed settings and a bit of aim work i was quickly bathed head to toe in the viscera of raiders | as good as this early game combat is was | the game suffers from a difficulty curve issue | in that curve based on level and location enemies will have higher health and better equipment | the issue that arises during most vanilla gameplay is the prevalence of 'bullet sponge' enemies | i found myself like many others frustrated to find that the headshot i landed in vats did little to put a dent in the malnourished pool cue wielding jet addicts i would frequently encounter | i was impressed with the options given to me regarding how i could customize settlements as well as the many options for weapon mods and armour crafting | the customization offered in the base game fallout is a long shot from the limited options of three and further expands upon the concepts and ideas that made new vegas unique | i applaud the reward of experience for building items and additions to settlements | 'roleplaying game' | in truth besides picking your character's name gender customizing their looks with one of the least intuitive face sculpting tools i have ever seen you are presented with very few opportunities or situations where you actions have consequences or change how the rest of the game plays out | allow me to explain: apart from the 'picking a side' aspect that they ripped off from fallout: new vegas very few quests present you the player with alternatives that affect how the quest ends | part of this may be due to the removal of the skills that all fallout games have had since fallout so many years ago but rarely do you decisions mean anything | the quests are very linear and rarely are you given an alternative method of completing them | additionally there are very few real quests | there are about radiant quests that consist of 'go to x location and kill x enemy' but thinking back now besides the faction-specific portions of the main quests i can only think of maybe real side quests that did not follow the formula i mentioned above | another major sticking point: exploration | while the infinitely repeating radiant quests seem specifically designed to introduce you the player to a location you haven't visited yet there is very little in trying to explore anything that doesn't have a map marker | gone are the fun hard to fine unmarked locations with hilarious easter eggs or unique loot there really just isn't | any of that | i am an avid free-roaming explorer and i was disappointed that so much of the unmarked space was so | empty and meaningless | sure they remember to toss some random static objects around but nothing you can collect nothing that is a challenge to locate and thus gives a sense of achievement for finding it | the underwater sections are the worst part of the free-roaming exploration aspect do not even bother looking for stuff underwater | even if there is a sunken ship it will not have any loot in in | i kept a tally and the number of actual lootable objects i found in the underwater sections of the exterior worldspace was | and every single one of them was very much so in the open and trivially easy to spot further cheapening any actual sense of meaningful accomplishment for finding it | now of the new features fallout was so eager to tote let's begin with base building | yes it is very fun at first | once you realize there are very view actual set pieces for you to build with and that the collision on them is so buggy that you can rarely actually build what you want with them it starts to feel very hollow | furthermore as the world opens up and you are given more settlements to babysit it starts to become too much to handle | i started groaning whenever i was given a new settlement and why | because you are now under the obligation to maintain it and defend it | so that just meant another hour of my time setting up the same prefab setup of defenses crops beds and water supply that i used for every base i did not actually care about | furthermore do not be fooled into thinking that the bases can fend for themselves | you will randomly get messages saying 'x settlement is under attack | ' and at that point you must drop everything and go help | it doesn't matter if the settlement being attacked is armed with missile turrets and a squad of guards wearing top of the line power armor and gatling lasers because of you don't show up the game just rolls a rng and 'decides' how much of you stuff to blow up regardless of any other factors | so even if you are loading screens down balls deep in a dungeon be prepared to drop everything you are doing and make a mad dash for the settlement that's being attacked | i properly defended all my settlements so % of the time when i was finished 'warping in' fast traveling the 'attack' was already over and i had 'won' before the screen even finished loading in and the attackers were nothing more than bloody smears on the cement | moving onto the second toted feature: gun mods | i will admit these were also fun at first | very quickly however i realized that in total there were about guns and melee weapons in fallout and while sure you can use weapon mods to make them behave a bit differently that's just too damn few | i quickly grew bored of every gun and could not use the strategy i used for previous fallout games when this happened go grab a new gun mod to try because even at the time of writing we the modders still haven't decoded the game enough to be able to add new unique weapons or armors to the game and this has nothing to do with the delay of the ckgeck which still won't be released for several months at least but because of all the changes that bethesda made to the | nif systems which they would not tell us about even after the tools have been released as bethesda has not released their true modding suite of dev tools since flipping morrowind relying on the community to come up with rd party hack tools to add new models to the game | and finally i would like to mention how much recycling bethesda did of previous game's asserts | while i know that todd howard said that fallout began with a port of skyrim to the xbone the sheer number of reused assets is rather disappointing and quite galling | want an easy to spot example | the 'wild dogs' use the entire skyrim wolf sound set from breathing to walking to attacking to death sounds it's all exactly % the same with zero changes | so many environment assets were ported directly from fallout fallout: new vegas as well without even bothering to give them an hd makeover so they look jarringly low poly and generally low grade and clash with the rest of the environment | and the creatures | once i thought about it i had a hard time coming up with a single creature that didn't either use a skyrim creature's skeleton rigging and animations or was just ported from fallout new vegas: deathclaws | werewolves | molerats | skeevers | blood bugs | chaurus hunters | yao guai | bears also with a % skyrim sound set and additional no model changes at all just some texture swaps ffs | radstags | elkdeer | all the robots | fallout new vegas ports besides maybe the new assultrons but they just use humanoid rigging anyways | bloatflies | fallout new vegas ports | radscorpions | fallout new vegas ports | mirelurks | fallout new vegas imports | mirelurk kings | fallout new vegas imports | super mutant behemoths | giants | super mutants | fallout new vegas ports with a few 'tweaks' | the only exceptions i can think of are the radroaches which at least had new attack animations made for them although the rest of their rigging and animations are fallout new vegas imports and the mirelurk hunters which look like they use a modified mudcrab rig with a few new animations | and then there's the sheer number of humanoid animations that are completely identical to the ones created for skyrim such as the ones for sitting down or a chair or lying down onto a bed etc | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- so do i recommend this game | well tentatively 'yes' but only because it's still better than most of the garbage coming out lately and whenif modding finally gets released there will be a lot of well made mods to add content to it as always | but you are honestly better off just playing fallout: new vegas to be perfectly honest |

compared to questions like does it hold up compared to previous titles in the series and is the story worthwhile | structurally it's a new breath in an old franchise; it takes a well established world and it questions what it is what makes it good | it takes a long standing tradition of robots that are inescapably non-human and breaches that divide | it pulls from titles like philip k | 's do androids dream of electric sheep and pays homage to the history of work it's trying to expand upon | like the other bethesdas it's the sort of game where you can walk to a random spot on the map and just start looking around | what's really good about the game is in the small stories hidden away in books and computers | the glowing sea is incredible i found myself timidly hovering over my screen gasping at the unnatural yellows and oranges of the landscape staring down my scope at any opportunity to ensure my path was clear | halfway through these desloate wastes i found myself with the same exhileration i had walking out of the vault for the first time all those years ago wandering into the strange and dangerous wasteland | i don't believe that the story and the character agency are on par with new vegas which is a very high mark but i think that it's made up for with the introduction of new mechanics | allowing the player total freedom to craft their settlements is a grand step | it allows the player to become attached to places since they're the one who built them | i'm looking forward to the eventual dlc |

review_text: first off fallout is my favourite franchise of all time that being said i'm not gonna be brown nosing bethesda as despite this game being great and being one i absoutely recommend it does have it's flaws which i will do my best to outline in this review | anyway onto the review | performance now my opinon is based on what experience i've had and my pc specs | they are as follows: cpu amd fx gpu nvidia geforce gtx ti gb ram gb ddr os windows home premium now at the time of this review the beta patch has been released optionally and one patch has gone through that solved a problem with audio | i've not experience any gaming breaking bugs or glitches that have forced me to start a new game or made the game unplayable | i've experience a few bugs like guns or my pipboy going invisbile which were easily solved by going into third person and back into first person again | the biggest glitch was when on my second play through i couldn't sleep on a bed in a settlement without the game freezing so i left the area then came back later and it was fine again | the game runs relatively smoothly for me on high settings with a few ultra settings thrown in there | only a few places such as downtown boston and places that cause a lot of shadows to be cast cause the most frame drops | the game looks good and does an amazing job of maintaining the retro feeling of s america with advanced technology and the game looks a lot more vibrant with bright and pastel colours and of course a barren yet beautiful looking wasteland | gameplay the gameplay has vastly improved compared to the previous two games such as the gunplay and npc combat ai | guns feel powerful even the mm pistol and they sound it too | characters from enemies to frendlies both seek cover and will do their best to flank you and kill you however they can sometimes be stupid for example i've seen raiders try to throw molotovs at me only for them to hit the cover they're behind and burn themselves instead | people feel that the gunplay was focused on more and so the game is just a glorified fps | people think this is because some of the rpg elements such as character customisation and dialogue have been ripped from the game and left bare | bethesda have opted for a dialogue system similar to mass effect which is another great game in my opinion and this leaves fallout's dialogue restricted to choices; yes no sarcastic and another option which usually asks for more information | there's also a voiced protagonist now for both male and female characters which i quite like and think the voice acting is well done for both the player and every other character | the character customization has also been changed extensively such as the possibilty now of having a fat character or super buff or really skinny | also hair with physics on them so they move as you do | skills have been scrapped though so now things like speech checks are reduced to how charismatic you are rather than how much skill you have in explosives for example | instead of skills your character is now decided by your specials and perks which only require levels and a certain amount of your special which if you're new to fallout stand for different stats : strength perception endurance charisma intelligence agility and luck | though this system is more restrictive in terms of character design it doesn't entirely limit what kind of character you can have you just have to look at the perk sheet to see what kind of perks you can get | people have also complained that your character already has a lot of their information already pre made for them for example the male is a military veteran father and husband and the female character is a law student mother and wife | though i can see where people come from when they say it's severely limiting fallout has never been a fully fleged rpg where you can design every single aspect of your character a lot of things have been pre deterimined | these arguements are mostly baseless as they're from the kind of people who want their character to either be some big breasted dumb as a sack of screws anime waifu piece of trash or and edgy evil super villian who only wears black hoods called 'shadow le deth' | you can still decide if you want your character to be the savior the wasteland deserves someone who wants to watch the world burn again or somewhere in between | however there's no longer a karma system in the game so it doesn't make a whole lot of difference other than how people react to you | a new feature they have added is the settlement builder which allows you to create and maintain your own settlements | as cool as this is the controls can be iffy at times and it will also take a lot of your time if you really get into it | it's also thrown onto you at the start of the game though it is optional it doesn't make much sense for you to have the knowledge of house building straight away | story and world the story's quality can be down to opinion mostly and mine is that it's great it drew me in kept me hooked and in some parts blew my mind but i'll not spoil the story | if you wanted to find it out you could of done but if not i'd say it's something you've got to experience for yourself | it's linear in some areas like the previous two games but there are still plenty of choices to make especially towards the end of the game when it can make a major difference towards the ending | also you can play after the ending unlike new vegas and base game fallout which they could of easily made it so that was a dlc released months later | the world has had great attention to detail kept throughout the entire commonwealth wasteland there's a lot of things left in the same place as they would have been when the world ended and landmarks of boston have been recreated which try to stay true to real life and what the lore would allow | some such landmarks include bunker hill fenway park mit or cit in the fallout universe and the uss constitution | there is still plenty to explore as there has been in previous games and another good thing about this game is that all of downtown boston is free from loading screens except for the interior locations however some buidlings you can enter without going through a loading door and these still have loot and other details in them | animation other things i was impressed by were the animations | dogmeat one of the possible companions had all of his animations based on a real dog so they could create more realistic movements and actions | another companion piper who also happens to be one of my favourites is first shown of to be doing some very eccentric actions when you first meet her rather than just being an idle body with a face that has only a moving mouth | this is true for pretty much every npc you find except maybe a few such as raiders which just sit or patrol | sound the music of this game is amazing both the game music and on the radio however the radios can seem quite limited as there's the radio which plays popular music of the atomic era and then there's the classical radio | the sound design is especially good as you can now here gunshots in the distance and they're different depending on what weapons are used and how far away they are or if they're behind a building | there's also different ambient sounds depending on your location so in an old wooden church you can hear the creaking of the wood or in a sewer drops of water on water with an echo if it's in a pipe for example | finally thank you if you read through all of this regardless of you agreeing with it or not | hopefully i've convinced you to buy this amazing game if not each is to their own |
