review_text: sigh lemme start out by saying that i love fallout | my first fallout game was and i enjoyed it and i loved new vegas even more it's pretty high on my favorite games of all time | i also enjoyed skyrim a bunch | i expected bethesda to take what obsidian did with new vegas bring it in and make it better | i didn't see much of it in the trailers and honestly the disappointment started to sink in | starting with the shoddy development of the dialogue wheel | i also noticed how skills were absent but i still had hope that the rest would be just fine and that there was good reason | i purchased the game on release downloaded it and started it up | immediately i had concerns about graphic customization being that it was far less sophisticated than what i could do with new vegas and fallout | still i pushed on with hopes that it would all work out fine | then i started my game and saw the opening video which in my opinion was excellently done and really hooked me | i also loved the idea of being someone who existed in the pre-war era who experiences the apocalypse years later | while it was rushed i realized that it was to keep the pacing | the face creation system is as good as it's ever been but it's a bit vague | from there on to exiting the vault i was in love | that love sunk faster than the titanic shortly after | now i'm going to break the game down | visuals and sounds: this is as good as fallout has ever looked but we all knew that they were re-using the same engine so it wasn't exactly top notch | it basically looks as good as new vegas with enbs and a ton of texture packs | the faces are also as good as fallout has looked along with some of the better animations i've seen bethesda crop up | soundwise it was spot on music again was nicely done kind of resembling fallout | this is the game's best part combat: this is another one of bethesda's biggest improvements | gunplay is as good as ever and the power armor system is awesome | the weapon modification system is solid af wonderful job there | sadly this seesm to be where beth devoted their time | armor modifications do make sense but i am disappointed by how they got rid of damage threshhold | gameplay: now this is where it goes wrong | immediately i notice that there's no option for hardcore mode one of my favorite additions to new vegas | also the karmareputation system is absent | this is one of the biggest sins i've seen | karma was flawed but it was a system that made sense in an rpg and reputation was another great addition by obsidian | with those gone i feared for how rpg mechanics in general would turn out | this also came through in leveling | perks are now purely combat and half of them are as useless as the ones in fallout | it's clear also that you can max everything out fairly quickly with no trouble and that's what frustrates me about an rpg as it eliminates the idea of playing to a certain style | dialogue: i dedicated this entire section to my frustration with it | the dialogue wheel is the worst addition to fallout | while it worked in mass effect it's poorly done here | all you get is options in every conversation with the same results: yes no sarcasticinfo maybe | it's disgraceful and we don't even get to see what we're about to say which forces us to rely on the voice action | the dialogue writing as well is completely one-dimensional boring and almost cringeworthy | when i heard the whole crap of 'destiny' from that stoner grandma i knew i was in for another cliche-ridden crap fest | story: and here's where i continue | having the motivation ofl ooking for the player's son is good but that motivation is gone when presented with a bunch of crap from other characters | the characters are clearly another step down reverting to the blackwhite dilemma of good versus evil | i know it gets into the whole idea of synths versus humans and morality but at the moment the momentum is just dead | oh and if you notice it's practically the same story as fallout and skrim and a bunch of other bethesda games: find what you lost i know bethesda isn't known for crafting great stories but that's what fallout is all about: the great story of the apocalypse | you're the next chapter | also you get the power armor at level | what kind of game design is that | power armor used to be a reward something you aspired to get | practically you're playing bethesda's character at this point not your own | rpg: this doesn't even deserve a section because this game has shifted from rpg with shooter mechanics to shooter with rpg mechanics | instead of innovating bethesda gutted what i loved about fallout and took the role playing out of rpg | you can trace this back to after morrowind though that they've been doing this | this actually starts at the well-written beginning because you're railroaded to be either a useless wife or a vet whom both are parents and are 'were one big happy family i must do this cause its necessary for my kid' in every conversation no matter what you do thus creating a split persona between you and the character you're playing which nullifies the idea of 'being whoever you want' | the fact that you get your own faction in the span of minutes is another insult | if my character gets follows that quickly no matter my charisma then i must be hitler | additionally pretty much every quest is fetch this shoot that go there | this continues my rant about dialogue in that we don't get to use attribues special for dialogue nor any skills | all that affects dialogue is charisma instead of using other attributes to affect what we say intelligence for smarts strength for bruteness etc | this goes hand in hand with the lack of the awesome reputation system from new vegas which made you want to get in bed with some people and kill others | you could almost call this false advertising because rpg values are like ghosts here | companions: i like how fluid the dog works and moves but i'm missing the companion wheel because it was so convenient and effective | a lot of what you can do with the dog is useless and distracting so it's just there to run around and chew on | the problem is that having a companion is annoying because it's hard to track them and they end up doing dumb stuff like before which you can't prevent | crafting: a great idea but this that i didn't give your game the obligatory because it's fallout | i forgot i'm supposed to blindly accept whatever bethesda throws my way | and for those of you who are saying hours isn't enough time believe me it was | if you can't get a solid opinion on a game in that timeframe then you just have issues | and even if i played longer i guarantee you that you all would be like 'derr then why do u play if u don like it' can't have it both ways | but to satisfy your rage i watched a few more hours worth of videos on the game and i still was not impressed | i even watched my friend play it on the ps and we both realized the truth: fallout is an utter disappointment please enjoy the show in the comments because the ragers have arrived |

review_text: a brief review on fallout : having played my own fair share of hours thus far i can say that fallout is a great game | it is far from a perfect game though | the main story spoilers is more of a side-trip from the exploration and discovery that is more commonly loved in bethesda rpgs | the gunplay is fantastic | it feels much better than that of fallout and definitely an upgrade from fallout nv | the weapons feel a lot more unique and the upgrade system works very well | the first time i used a gauss rifle was amazing as the charge mechanic was very satisfying when ripping through a deathclaw or super mutant | the removal of skill points as a determining factor is probably for the best | a lot of people complain that it makes it much harder to change up your character think the system works better | lastly the map | a fairly large number of people complained about how small the map seemed at first but i can tell you from experience that the map is huge | while the area of the map might not seem like much it is a very dense map often having loads of buildings and ruins to explore in any parts | being the type that loves the sniper builds it was fantastic to have clumsy nord | this was in part due to design decisions and also due to developer overlooks | the removal of athletics and acrobatics removed an entire playstyle that allowed your character to be agile thing that really irks me about these questlines is that they all just devolve into random dungeon crawls | i counted: you only need to use magic thrice in the mages guild | advancing through the guild has nothing to do with actually using magic or being skilled | you're just watching a poorly developed story unfold not rising through the ranks of an esteemed guild of scholars | there's no way to distinguish your character or give him a personality through dialogue or your race class | this was a stark difference from fallout and new vegas where your perks gave you extra dialogue options and could change entire questlines and you could choose dialogue options that really gave your character an interesting personality | skyrim game seems afraid to give you any consequences | argonians aren't allowed in windhelm | except for you | khajiit aren't typically trusted in the cities | funny no one even seems to realize i'm a khajiit in the first place | not even a unique quest for argonian players to gain entrance into the city | you may say 'this would've been too hard for the devs to implement' but it makes me wonder why they present these plot-points into the game if they're not willing to actually follow through with them | there's not even a single mention of your race throughout the entire game other than the occassional quip from a bandit | my altmer was walking by some dominion soldiers and i was surprised they didn't even have any unique dialogue | they just treated me like i was a nord and shooed me off not even scolding me for being a 'traitor' to my kind | entire quests could have been more unique by acknowledging the unique aspects of my player instead of pretending they don't exist | the quests give you the illusion that you'll be able to influence the world or change things then snatch away the opportunity at the last minute | the civil war for example: no matter who you side with no high king will ever be crowned and no one in the world will ever acknowledge the war is over | in the markarth quest you can side with the forsworn but there are no consequences | the forsworn will still be hostile to you and nothing ever comes of your allegiance | you can come up with any excuse you want to explain these things but the fact remains that bethesda chose not to take these choices further | so what you're left with is a shallow dungeon crawler with a lackluster combat system removal of many rp aspects a weak narrative and | well that's it | i know the other games had issues too but i expect a developer's work to improve over time | under control | morrowind had a lot of issues and is incredibly outdated but for what it was i think that it did a better job of this than skyrim | in skyrim i just feel like i'm on soft-rails in an open world watching the pretty killcams and interacting with the world but i never felt like a living person in a living world | tl;dr the only saving grace for skyrim are the mods but they often there are no challenging fights or platforming scenes you can ramp up the difficulty at the start of the play through but the lack of being able to change this on the fly once you have started is disappointing | like i said boss fights usually conclude in quick time events and regular enemy fights are nothing other than a time filler as they offer no challenge what-so-ever | i finished the game in just under four hours; gutteral voice brooding angst and a hood worn far too low over the face | i was pleasantly surprised to find starkiller's demeanor to be far more relateable and altogether human | a little over halfway through the game after listening to the old jedi and the young jedi bicker like a married couple each pouting and throwing fits at various intervals their personalities began to grate on me | i found the most overall pleasant character to be the love interest and she was offscreen roughly % of the game | to be honest though our two protagonists were still much less flat and unlikeable than i expected so i can't be too harsh | as far as gameplay is concerned it wasn't anything particularly unique | it felt like a hack n' slash with superpowers think god of war but less interesting | i think all of your force powers are unlocked within the first quarter of the game which meant that you had plenty of time to master and upgrade the ones you wanted and ignore the ones you didn't but unfortunately there wasn't really enough of a selection to make combat really feel like your own | you are given virtually no variability as far as melee combos which is a little disappointing since i occasionally like to feel like i'm doing more than just mashing the attack button until a finishing move happens | the game tries to present the player with some customization with the unlockable saber crystals but honestly once i locked in the ones that gave me more force points i didn't even bother anymore | i will readily acknowledge the pleasure in using force powers to mow down scores of stormtroopers turn lightsaber wielding baddies against their friends and redirect projectiles at whatever other enemy the arbitrary targeting system for force throw decides go for which is another gripe i have | the inclusion of quicktime events as all but mandatory is frustrating | getting to watch our hero dismember robots in spectacular ways is very very cool; i found my mouth slightly agape the first time i watched starkiller detonate the hulking fire droid | watching our hero do the same exact thing dozens of times because it is the quickest way to finish off those enemies however turns into a chore pretty quickly | the length of the game for me was about hours which felt brief given the lack of replayability in the design but i do think the game knew when to quit since the gameplay hadn't gotten the chance to become intolerably stale before i hit the ending sequence | the game did not know however how to challenge the player once a grasp has been gotten on how to use the op jedi | i never really felt more than marginally challenged by the game and the platforming section near the end of the game posed more difficulty than the actual final faceoff which was a joke of a fight and that's funny given how admittedly bad i am at video games | the ease of play mixed with some of the semi-interactive non-combat sequences of force feats manage to really make the player feel the power of the force that is dwelling within starkiller and it's always fun to feel like a superhero but those looking for a challenge will find themselves crawling back to dark souls so they can feel human or hollow again | all in all i had a very good time playing the game | i never really felt bored though i never felt very challenged either | the game feels like it was built for youngsters that are a fan of the series rather than seasoned gamers that are looking for something deep or immersive | if you are a fan of star wars or a fan of hack and slash gameplay with a throw-away plot then i would recommend you buy it just not for full price |

can't walk faster than a hurried trot | it's been a while since i've played the first one but in this one my movement felt hamstrung | enemies: just as in the first game enemies eventually cope with your god-like powers by being magically immune to some of them though this is usually less annoying than it is the first time around | i wonder where vader's armies of secret force-immune warriors and missile-toting robots went by the beginning of a new hope | boss fights tend to have incredibly simple patterns and yet drag on endlessly | level design: there are a few interesting set-pieces in this extremely linear game but too often the design slows you down with endless and very dull jumping and locking mechanism 'puzzles' that really do nothing but delay your progress with pointless tedium | overall art direction is ok with a fair amount of work put into some levels and not so much into others | story: anyone who played the first game knows that the force unleashed story is totally ridiculous but serviceable given that they're just trying to write some kind of plot around the fun gameplay gimmick of being an ultra-powerful jedi | despite what a cheesy tie-in it was it felt epic in its own way | this time around though the writers completely phoned it in | nothing is explained if you haven't played the first game and makes little sense even if you did | the plot is extremely character asks the other's name | in terms of storytelling depth it feels like a half-baked dlc add-on for the first game at best | that may be a generous assessment | the game is noticeably short even compared to the fairly short first game | music: about the same as before with an ost consisting of exactly one musical sting for your character | all other music is recycled john williams score review_text: i bought this game elsewhere for $ at the end of february to see if it ran and thankfully it's a ton of fun overall | even the low settings look really good from the expansive environments to the detailed vehicles and character faces obviously minus some texture detail | framerate drops during outdoor gliding and driving at high speeds are frequent but not usually crippling | crashes were very rare | load times tend to be short or masked with elevator rides though there's a notable lightshadow glitch in one small indoor-outdoor area that can be tilted back and forth | moving on from the infamous optimization the game places the tried-and-true arkham mechanics in an open and gorgeous gotham city that doesn't feel nearly as cramped as arkham city did | the often typical story still does its job decently and is sometimes genuinely touching | scarecrow threatens to unleash his 'fear gas' prompting an evacuation of gotham and leaving behind batman the police department several villains lots of thugs and many other characters who need to be rescued | much of the plot involves batman trying to stop scarecrow or dealing with the problems inside his own head that are still left over from arkham city as well as fending off a new villain dubbed the arkham knight a fully masked figure who wants revenge on batman for 'something | ' beyond the gliding and perching stealth sections that are largely similar to previous games in the series now with more outdoor stealth which looks great much of the game revolves around driving the batmobile which has a default 'car' mode for chasing and a separate 'tank' mode that's capable of strafing | the vehicle has a lot of weight and though its handling and controls take time to get used to it can navigate tight corners | driving a tank obviously isn't very smooth or graceful but the drone fights which should have been called 'bat-tlezone' give you a nice handicap | enemies telegraph where their attacks will land with targeting lasers | navigate a maze of these lasers and shoot at drones over and over | build up combos without getting hit to temporarily unlock devastating abilities sound familiar | the game later adds slow-paced car-stealth sections that feel like old splinter cell against heavy tanks | i preferred the mounted stealth in mordor's 'lord of the hunt' expansion which required care but also allowed you to feel powerful instead of repeatedly biding your time as the underdog | highway chases are much more exciting as your car can lock onto enemies while you drive allowing you to shoot missiles at them with a button press and a gratifying burnout-style crash camera | other challenges involve races or unorthodox puzzles such as an early section that's basically 'car of persia' complete with a flythrough camera showing you where to go | some of the optional side challenges are much more frustrating than most anything in the main story but are part of a leaderboard system you can compete against steam friends with | plowing into thugs or sending their occupants flying out the sides as no-kill batman looks silly though | melee combat feels as much like tony hawk with thugs' faces as it ever did but now there are tag fights with funny dialogue and a better variety of enemies including medics who revive enemies and several large foes who can't simply be punched | the old dodge-strike-dodge-strike pattern usually still works even on knightmare difficulty but you can't grind experience by beating up random thugs outside of missions | the predator sections got the most noticeable upgrade in the new fear multi-takedown system | splinter cell: conviction was noted for being similar to arkham asylum and knight feels like it's returning the favor in giving batman a new mechanic that must be earned to use as with sam fisher's executions | instead of pre-selecting targets though you attack them one by one in slow motion similarly to the teleport strike from shadow of mordor | for the sake of balance batman can only do this once per fight unless he silently and slowly takes down another foe | knockout smashes don't count | you can also throw a limited number of gadgets while gliding into a melee fight but i rarely needed to | there are a few dozen roadside checkpoints to neutralize which have a thoughtful variety of layouts but can become exhausting | there are two big issues i have with the fear takedown: if it were usable in cutscenes a good chunk of the plot could probably be skipped and as mentioned the balance and level design become silly when you can often take down five guys at once grapple to the first high point you see put a solo goon to sleep and repeat | the game's missions are generally fair about your opposition: if you have to be on foot or drive your enemies ~usually~ do the same | detective puzzles return and are fun but a bit rare | the story is fine but seems to rely on its twists and 'gotchas' to maintain interest which would have worked better if many were given time to actually be emotional before being cancelled out | one only felt necessary because of the gameplay but another was brutally effective even though i myself had it spoiled elsewhere | parents of younger series fans may want to know that the game does earn its mature rating even without injecting gore into fights and that the beginning and especially the end of the story are so immensely violent that they effectively change genres | the two most annoying things about the story by far are both in the title | batman insists on doing nearly everything himself is often ungrateful when he does receive help even in no-win situations and is ruthlessly bossy | i laughed out loud during the arkham knight's ultimate identity 'reveal | ' he's very whiny though it must be said that his final fight like many here was neat if repetitive | challenge maps are back; 'beyond batman' there's a skin for that you can usually play as two of his helpers along with catwoman and a freaking cool fourth bonus character who also shows up during the story | villain banter and other speech simulation activated during challenges are incredibly repetitive simulation failed especially when the arkham knight is yelling | you'll lose track of how often thugs tell you to 'grow a pair' even when you're playing as catwoman who most decidedly has | regardless if you want to see wayne manor and to revisit the asylum sanatorium here you go | along with the concept art numerous well-written short stories and d model showcases there's also a photo mode which allows you to pause gameplay or cutscenes and apply a variety of filters and other effects | i don't think you can play the whole game in black and white or neon colors but you can still review_text: look past its shaky pc release and barring some compatability flaws arkham knight is a thoroughyl enjoyable batman game in the vein of its predecessors | while maintaining the same formula multi-takedowns both in stealth and in combat have been changed to feel more free-flowing and more empowering to the player while the addition of the batmobile adds even more versatility in traversing the city | also worth noting is a more vibrant and living breathing representation of gotham as opposed to the very lifeless arkham city the overworld itself not the game | the primary drawbacks of the game came from the game's over-reliance on batmobile-based puzzles which really didn't need to use it and the monotony of % completion yes ridder trophies once again | the batmobile challenges and puzzles often boil down to driving it to point a attaching a winch and tapping a button at increasing speeds; while combat very quickly becomes as boring as the most generic of shooters on the market | in addition there are times when the batmobile must be used counter-productive to how puzzles would be solved in past games | the easiest example to call to mind is batman stating early on 'the bat-claw won't cut it i'll need to use the batmobile winch' despite being able to literally pull down walls with the bat-claw in previous games | % completion truly left a bad taste in my mouth this time however | the game did draw from some a-list and b-list and even d-list batman villains but most of these were entertaining fresh and unique in their own way and then there's the riddler | for the third time this green has scattered a bunch of t around gotham except to the effect of around riddler trophies and challenges | now the game also has a very entertaining feature where the villains 'still active' in gotham will openly taunt you over gotham's speakers led screens and video sign-boards: for some appaulling reason riddler appears far too often and after successively jailing each other active villain this only compounds the problem: an approximate hours of tedium accompanied by a whiny idiot whose voice you literally cannot avoid every minutes | to make matters worse since many riddler challenges also involve the batmobile the game cleverly disguises loading screens under elevator sequences: the problem being that what is used during these elevator sequences is another diatribe by the riddler | gripes aside give arkham knight a chance | the story is phenomenal and has some amazing and truly entertaining moments especially the game's finale | as a fan of the comics and of batman i highly recommend arkham knight if not on pc then on console |

review_text: overall this was great fun to play | if you've played any of the other batman: arkham games then you know what you're in for and this shouldn't disappoint | the combat feels very refined and more forgiving so you can feel more like batman than ever | the 'tag team' boss fights where you're joined by one or another of batman's crimefighting or criminal partners also play really well | the batmobile features prominently with several races and car vs drone fights and the mechanics are decent | the huge difference in firepower between the bat and the batmobile makes for an uneven experience with the fights though taking on a batman fight with the batmobile is completely one-sided and the game throws up some awkward hints if you're not in the car but are in over your head 'it's ok guys the batman is outnumbered and we're safe from his batmobile behind this large destructible wall' | the story is interesting and well delivered but a lot of pivotal moments feel a bit contrived or out of character including a couple of really awful 'press x to do this thing that you don't really want your character to do' events | the biggest let-down for me is the balance between the main storyline the side quests and the open world | the open world no longer rewards you with experience or anything else for roaming the streets and 'delivering justice' to random groups of thugs so out nearly verbatim that you won't be able to continue the main quest until you complete more side quests and many of the side quests are also gated so that you can't make progress until you complete x% of the main story | for a game set in such an open world this makes the game feel extremely linear | worst of all the 'true ending' is locked out until you take out every major villain in the game which includes 'solving' every one of the riddler's riddlescollectibles | i had fun with the riddler side quest in every other arkham game but being forced into it made it feel like such a chore | after several hours of making very slow progress i gave up and used someone else's saved game instead | there's a lot of fun to be had in the journey here but reaching the destination is
